episodes.request: How does ledgerline handle a quoted field with a comma in it, like "Dentist, check-up"? Just explain, please don't change anything.

steps.thought: The CSV code is in src/csv.ts.
Find where the example ledgers use quotes.

finish.report: splitLine in src/csv.ts walks the line one character at a time. A double quote switches quoting on and off, commas inside quotes stay part of the field, and a doubled quote inside a quoted field becomes one literal quote. examples/march.csv has one such field, the "Dentist, check-up" description. I changed nothing.

episodes.request: How does ledgerline lay out the tables it prints, and how are negative amounts shown? Just explain, please don't change anything.

steps.thought: See which modules call the table renderer.

finish.report: renderTable in src/format.ts sizes every column to its widest cell, separates columns with two spaces, left-aligns the first column, right-aligns the others, and trims trailing spaces from each line. formatCents turns a number of cents into a plain decimal with two places, so 123456 becomes 1234.56; a negative amount keeps a leading minus sign in front of the whole part, as in -12.05. I changed nothing.

episodes.request: How does ledgerline read a CSV row, and what is reported when a row has the wrong number of fields? I only want an explanation.

steps.thought: Look at the error class used for bad data.

finish.report: parseLedger in src/csv.ts drops blank lines, checks that the first line is date,category,description,amount, and then splits each row with splitLine. A row with a number of fields other than four raises a DataError whose message names the file and line number, such as ledger:3: expected 4 fields, found 3. It also rejects a bad date and an amount that is not a plain decimal. DataError is defined in src/errors.ts next to UsageError. I changed nothing.
